claims.heading: Product Goals
claims.text:
- A user can ask why a file changed and trace the answer to a UI action, tool
  call, trigger run, scheduler script, or unknown external change.
- A user can restore a file version even when the relevant harness context is
  buried, lost, interrupted, or unrelated to Git status.
- A user can inspect whether a failure came from the assistant, a trigger,
  a scheduler, an external editor, a filesystem operation, or app UI behavior.
- File and folder changes can refresh rendered views without destroying the
  current DOM, selection, scroll, active tab, or navigation state.
- Future background workers can review conversations, tool calls, file changes,
  and outcomes to surface concrete improvement suggestions.
- Future self-improvement loops can evaluate whether agents followed prompts,
  whether skills would be better than ad hoc instructions, and where the app can
  optimize repeated workflows.

claims.heading: Developer-Level Principles
claims.text:
- Events are facts after something happened. Commands may cause events, but the
  Universal Event Bus is not a request/response API.
- Provenance must separate observation from causation. Chokidar can observe a
  file change; it usually cannot prove who caused it.
- Direct initiators should carry durable IDs in `provenance.cause`: UI action
  IDs, tool call IDs, harness ID/run/event IDs, trigger run IDs, script run IDs,
  scheduler run IDs, automation run IDs, agent run IDs, or audit query IDs.
  Chat thread IDs, chat turn IDs, resource event IDs, root/parent event IDs, and
  correlation IDs belong under `ids`, domain payloads, or ledger edges.
- Unknown external changes should stay honest. If a change was not linked to UI,
  assistant, trigger, scheduler, script, or known system work, the ledger should
  mark it external or unknown instead of guessing.
- Resource/render sync and file versioning should consume the same canonical
  events. Views should not build isolated listener paths that drift from ledger
  provenance.
- Ledger subscribers can filter, compact, and summarize. Producers should
  preserve facts and avoid discarding metadata before subscribers can decide what
  matters.
- High-frequency file changes need storm control. The system must preserve that
  a storm happened without flooding the ledger or future assistant context.

claims.heading: Boundaries
claims.text:
- Producers emit facts with enough metadata for subscribers to decide relevance.
- Subscribers filter, compact, persist, broadcast, or trigger follow-up work.
- Canonical candidates pass schema validation or a validated-or-diagnosed publisher before canonical-only subscribers act. Record validation never becomes authorization or failure of the already-valid source operation.
- Canonical publication accepts only a privately registered `PreparedCanonicalCandidate`. `prepareCanonicalCandidate` strips caller-supplied proof fields, consumes upstream refs, and privately proves each registered atomic accepted-only relationship group. A missing, copied, stale, forged, mismatched, wrong-workspace, or otherwise unbound proof omits the whole affected relationship group with fixed value-free diagnostic `accepted_relationship_unbound`; it does not suppress an otherwise valid relationship-free base fact or affect the source operation. Whole-candidate suppression is reserved for an invalid required fact core, an unsanitizable base after relationship removal, an unrelated final schema error, or UEB failure. Admission clones/freezes the safe event, binds its allowlisted identity to an opaque ref, and freezes one `{ acceptedRef }` context. Every D01-admitted listener task calls exact ABI `listener(frozenEvent, deliveryContext)` with the same event/context/ref; bare-ref argument two is invalid. UEB returns `{ published: true, acceptedRef }` before listener code. Identity-sensitive consumers require `assertAcceptedDelivery`. A false publication result exposes no event/ref/context and queues nothing. Legacy `emit()` is non-migrated only.
- Source commands never await admission or a ref. A private per-command slot exposes only leased non-blocking `peekAccepted()` to frozen-registry producers. Command/producer `finally` paths close/release it; late/pending/terminal branches omit relationships, and private state is deleted only after close, terminal admission, and zero leases. SPEC-40 owns the exact slot API and race tests.
- Async listener chains preserve depth/trigger context across `await` boundaries using async-scoped context rather than process-global synchronous state. Concurrent root emissions remain isolated. Subscriber throws/rejections are logged and do not revoke an already true publish result.
- Resource sync, ledger persistence, metadata collectors, and future versioning consume accepted canonical events. TRIGGERS.md file-change execution remains on its one fail-open workspace-watcher path; mutation handlers do not add a second matcher, and canonical automation/resource events observe and correlate it without authorizing execution.
- New watchers or private event buses should not be added when the existing UEB pipeline can carry the event.

- `origin`: the initiating actor or context that caused work.

claims.heading: Metadata Must Not Gate Valid Work
claims.text:
- Authentication, authorization, command shape, required mutation target, workspace resolution, and path safety are operational checks. They may reject an unsafe command before it executes.
- Missing or malformed provenance context, attribution IDs, active-view fields, cause links, native references, enrichment, hashes, token counts, ledger availability, or versioning availability must not reject, delay, roll back, or suppress an otherwise valid operation.
- Canonical IDs and timestamps that the server controls are generated by the accepting producer. Do not require the renderer to manufacture them as a condition of interaction.
- When attribution cannot be established, use `external` or `unknown` with honest confidence. When enrichment cannot be captured, use the schema's omission/unavailable form. When no trustworthy canonical provenance record can be built, emit a structured non-canonical diagnostic and continue the operation.
- A provenance, ledger, versioning, compaction, or audit subscriber failure is isolated from the source operation. It may retry/defer only under its owner-approved bounded idempotency policy, otherwise it skips/terminates its own record with a fixed diagnostic; it must not make the already-valid source action fail. Ledger production retry/defer remains blocked on `LED-D04`.
- Redaction failure fails closed for sensitive material by omitting that material or its derived hash/preview. It never fails the source operation. Whether a non-sensitive event core is canonical depends on the domain registry: only an explicitly registered failure-safe-core branch may be admitted.

claims.heading: Boundary
claims.text: The renderer sends tentative non-ID active view, panel, tab, document, route, selected resource path, and similar UI context known at command time. The accepting server captures workspace ID/root/transition from the coordinator's `WorkspaceCommandContextRef`; session workspace/root fields are caches only. Renderer context/resources qualify only when the exact private workspace token binds to that same command ref and the server re-resolves paths/targets under it. The client token lives only in one memory-only slot keyed by the exact current OPEN WebSocket, outside all state caches and persistence, and is synchronously cleared on init/switch replacement, close, disconnect, socket replacement, and shutdown. First-package `ui.action` is a root canonical fact and omits root, parent, and causation IDs; any future UI relationship requires an exact SPEC-40 candidate/source selector and accepted capability. The server attempts an optional fresh correlation for the new chain. Successful generation inserts it through a private fresh-correlation binding; generator absence/throw, allocation, or registration failure omits only `ids.correlationId`, reports fixed `fresh_correlation_unavailable`, and leaves the otherwise safe UI fact and command unchanged. claims.heading: Topics And Canonical Payloads
claims.text: Migrated canonical publication accepts only an opaque `PreparedCanonicalCandidate`, canonical-clones/deep-freezes its safe event, binds its allowlisted identity to an opaque ref, and freezes one `{ acceptedRef }` context. `prepareCanonicalCandidate` is the sole accepted-only relationship constructor: it consumes upstream refs, inserts registered event/domain IDs, and records private pointer/ref proof; copying an `inspectAcceptedRef` string is insufficient. Every task uses exact ABI `listener(frozenEvent, deliveryContext)` with the same event/context/ref; bare-ref argument two is invalid. Identity-sensitive consumers use `assertAcceptedDelivery`. Mismatched, forged, unbound, or raw relationships fail. False admission exposes no event/ref/context and queues nothing. Tasks re-enter async chain context.

claims.heading: Failure Isolation
claims.text: Canonical publication is a provenance side effect, not command authorization, success, or a prerequisite to execution. After operational validation accepts a command, the operational path starts before initiating provenance is submitted to the supervised admission executor; the command/response chain never invokes or awaits provenance or an accepted-ref promise. Downstream producers use an already-filled command-scoped ref slot or omit the relationship without waiting. Mutation facts do not exist before the owning mutation succeeds; their provenance/recovery work is scheduled only after success and outside the mutation result/response chain. Missing metadata follows the omission/diagnostic path without lookup or retry.

claims.heading: Failure Isolation
claims.text: The command slot is a private per-command object, never keyed by renderer IDs. Only frozen-registry producers can acquire leases while the command scope is open. `peekAccepted()` is non-blocking; pending/terminal/late branches return no ref. Producers release leases in `finally`, the command closes acquisition in `finally`, and the supervised admission task always settles or runs its cancellation finalizer. Slot/ref state is deleted only after close, terminal admission, and zero leases. Exact APIs, reasons, races, and tests are normative in SPEC-40.

claims.heading: Failure Isolation
claims.text: Optional enrichment is used only when already available. After admission, UEB enqueues every listener as a separate supervised-executor task; it never calls listener code in the admission/source-operation stack or awaits returned promises. All callbacks are queued before task execution, each task re-enters the captured async-chain context, and rejections are diagnosed with deterministic test draining. Subscriber callbacks must use async I/O and offload unbounded CPU work; synchronous filesystem/database/provider I/O is forbidden. Ledger, versioning, audit, compaction, and other subscribers cannot hold the operation response open. Failures or unavailable dependencies never reject, delay, roll back, or rewrite the source result.

- thread managers own thread metadata, chat file mirrors, and any durable
  mirror-deletion recovery journal needed after a SQLite delete

- metadata services own saved exchange metadata patches
- workspace services own workspace registry and state cache writes
- a thread-group domain service owns visible-thread membership, primary-role
  history, visible-list MRU/activity events, and group-level mutations while
  preserving normal thread-manager mirrors for every session it creates
- view-state services own group-keyed content worksurfaces in each view
  capsule's `state/state.json`

claims.heading: Durable identity boundaries
claims.text:
- A view capsule's immutable identity is `metadata.view-id` in `manifest.md`,
  qualified by `workspaceId`. The target capsule root is
  `ai/<machine>/System/Views/`. Folder name, numeric prefix, ordering, and
  display name may change without changing that identity.
- A visible thread group owns membership, ordering, title, ranked collection
  assignments, view binding, and current-primary history in SQLite. Archive is
  a derived projection when no assignment is valid; do not add a separate
  archive-status owner. A nullable binding denotes the workspace Legacy host;
  it must not be filled from the active view and owns no view worksurface.
  Group `updated_at`, backed by idempotent accepted-user-activity records, is
  the visible-list MRU owner; session compatibility timestamps must not order
  group-backed rails.
- An underlying `threads` row owns one chat session and its transcript/runtime
  identity. Creating one must use `ThreadManager` or a transaction-capable
  primitive owned by `ThreadManager`, including the Markdown mirror and
  session-limit policy. Another domain service must not copy those invariants.
  Within `harness_config`, portable `model`/`variant` selection and provider
  session/runtime binding remain separate allowlisted namespaces even if they
  share one serialized column. Clone-like creation may copy only a server-
  validated portable selection; client input cannot populate provider identity,
  credentials, resume state, unknown keys, or retired Fork fields.
- The owning view capsule stores content worksurfaces. Do not duplicate those
  snapshots in the thread-group tables.

claims.heading: Protected System target boundary
claims.text:
System is intended to be readable but not directly writable by agents.
OpenCode is the first explicitly named protected harness; the same rule applies
to later harnesses. New code must keep every System mutation behind a narrow
Fusion-owned service and must not expose that service as generic file access to
a harness. Configuration and permission changes require a trusted,
user-mediated UI path. Automatic application state writes may use dedicated
state services, but they do not confer configuration or filesystem mutation
authority.

claims.text:
When one user action changes both SQLite thread structure and file-backed view
state, the SQLite transition includes a durable projection-outbox instruction,
not a duplicate view-state snapshot. The view-state write follows through its
normal service and acknowledges that instruction. If it fails, the command
reports the committed structure and marks view-state repair required; it does
not roll back by hand or leave an ambiguous primary.

claims.text:
Recovery retries only unapplied outbox instructions with an idempotency key. Do
not reconstruct every historical placement from membership/history: doing so
would resurrect tabs the user intentionally closed. A crash between applying
view state and acknowledging the outbox is safe because replay focuses or
preserves the existing tab rather than duplicating it.

claims.text:
Deleting SQLite chat/session rows does not make filesystem mirror cleanup
recoverable by itself. Before the canonical rows disappear, the thread manager
must durably retain each mirror identity in its own deletion journal (or an
equivalent manager-owned reconciliation index), then retry failed removals after
restart until applied. A view-state projection outbox is not a substitute for
the manager's transcript-mirror cleanup owner.

claims.heading: Cross-store recovery
claims.text:
Before deleting a thread group, the group service acquires a deletion lease and
the runtime owner proves every member is terminal and fully drained. A busy
member causes a non-mutating failure. Successful deletion fences every member's
runtime generation before the database transaction so late provider or event
frames cannot append exchanges, recreate runtime state, or publish a ghost
result. A Legacy group uses the same runtime and mirror rules but creates no
view-state cleanup projection.

claims.text:
That deletion lease is the exclusive group-mutation lease used by every
membership/primary-changing action. Move and Delete cannot interleave: the
winner completes its transaction before the loser enumerates or creates a
member, and both revalidate group/membership state inside their transaction.

vocabulary.text: After operational validation accepts a command, the operational command path starts before initiating provenance such as `ui.action` is submitted to the supervised admission executor. The command/response chain never calls or awaits construction, redaction, validation, admission, or an accepted-reference promise. Downstream producers bind a ref only when the command-scoped slot is already filled; otherwise they omit the relationship and diagnose without waiting. A `resource.*` fact exists only after the owning mutation succeeds; resource provenance/recovery work is scheduled after that success and outside its result/response chain. Optional enrichment is included only when already available. After admission and only under owner-approved `UEB-D01`, UEB offers each eligible listener as a separate bounded supervised-executor task in deterministic order. Admitted tasks re-enter captured async-chain context and observe returned-promise rejections; saturation independently skips/finalizes only the affected delivery, and one callback never prevents later callbacks from being offered under D01's fairness rules. Subscriber synchronous filesystem/database/provider I/O is forbidden.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Canonical publication accepts only a private `PreparedCanonicalCandidate`. `prepareCanonicalCandidate` strips caller proof fields, consumes upstream refs, inserts each fully proven registered atomic relationship group, and records private pointer/ref proof; copying the same string from `inspectAcceptedRef` is insufficient. Missing, mismatched, stale, forged, wrong-workspace, unbound, or raw proof omits the whole affected group with exact `accepted_relationship_unbound` while an otherwise valid relationship-free base fact remains eligible. Whole-candidate suppression is limited to invalid required fact core, an unsanitizable base after relationship removal, unrelated final schema error, or UEB failure. UEB admission clones/freezes the safe event, binds its registered identity to an opaque ref, and freezes one `{ acceptedRef }` context. Every admitted listener task uses exact ABI `listener(frozenEvent, deliveryContext)` with the same event/context/ref; bare-ref argument two is invalid and identity-sensitive consumers use `assertAcceptedDelivery`. A false publication result exposes no event/ref/context and queues nothing. Loop keys use the frozen identity's `eventId`; admitted tasks re-enter captured async context.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Operational file-change trigger predicates use the closed watcher key set and exhaustive byte/operand grammar defined by SPEC-32, including signed safe integers for negative `delta`, bounded no-escape strings, and null only for `ext|oldPath|newPath`. Unknown/canonical/provenance keys or any invalid combination reject only that file block before evaluation and never default true. Slice 32e side-effect-free parses/classifies mixed trigger files, validates file blocks, and atomically replaces watcher filters. Cron and bus blocks never use this grammar and retain their one-time registration lifecycle; workspace reload cannot duplicate/remove them. Workspace parse failure installs no old-root filters, while same-workspace fatal reload retains the last valid set. Optional provenance is correlation-only after execution.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: The complete file-block schema is closed. Slice 32e alone owns watcher repoint/recompile; Slice 32d preserves the current matcher and cannot assume the new controller. Slice 32e loads immutable base filter descriptors once, but instantiates declarative actions and workspace-side-effecting programmatic factories per opaque watcher `{workspaceRoot,generation}`. The controller owns unforgeable generation capabilities. After RSC-D16 closes, synchronous entry to the Slice-32b0 coordinator's watcher hook verifies the next ordered transition pair, makes B/null current, irreversibly invalidates A, attaches B handlers, starts supervised/watchdog-bounded A-close/B-ready/reconciliation, and returns a non-Promise acknowledgment. Those tasks never hold the coordinator; A completion cannot regain currency, and current ready/reconciliation failure or expiry enters bounded `degraded_recovery_pending` plus exactly one direct freshness recovery. Every action checks currency before work, after every await/callback boundary, and immediately before each irreversible effect. Timers/queued callbacks retain the capability and stale ones no-op. Atomic replacement preserves descriptor identity while preventing startup-root closure reuse; B effects target only B. Concurrent requests become adjacent coordinator transitions, obsolete or never-settling work cannot affect/block the next generation, and reconciliation never synthesizes trigger execution. Workspace trigger reload cannot affect cron/bus listeners.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Open owner decision `RSC-D16` blocks Slice 32e. It must approve exact positive millisecond watchdogs for old-watcher close diagnostics, current-generation readiness, and reconciliation; monotonic clock/timer/config/test ownership; minus/exact/plus boundary behavior; cancellation on generation change/shutdown; and diagnostic/recovery dedupe. Ready/reconciliation expiry enters `degraded_recovery_pending` and issues exactly one current-generation freshness recovery; close expiry is cleanup diagnostic only. No default may be invented and no watchdog participates in provenance or blocks the workspace FIFO.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: `ULV-D12` remains an owner-decision blocker before 40b2d1 or any non-batch canonical file-version emission/persistence. It must define the exact file-version event types; phase/lifecycle and common-envelope presence/status; ID/actor/provenance/context/resource/redaction/omission matrices; identity and idempotency; deterministic bounds; ordering/dedupe/replay/retry/restart; safe failure forms; and subscriber/ledger transaction boundaries. Conceptual optional, `unknown`, or generic-record sketches supply no defaults.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Root event, parent event, thread, turn, correlation, and causation IDs belong under `ids`. `provenance.cause` is reserved for schema-approved durable upstream initiator IDs such as UI action, tool call, harness ID/run/event, automation run, or audit query IDs. Trigger/scheduler/script/agent subtype causes remain `AUT-D03`/finding-1 candidates rather than settled common fields.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: The renderer token exists only in one module-private memory slot keyed by the exact current WebSocket object. It is excluded from Zustand, workspace/panel/view caches, state pushes, browser/Electron persistence, URL/history, and every serialized snapshot. Init/switch clears before optional install; a metadata-only update installs only on exact current socket/workspace/root equality; close, explicit disconnect, socket replacement, and shutdown clear synchronously before another prompt read or reconnect scheduling. Prompts read only for the current OPEN socket. After owner-approved `RSC-D17`, server allocation runs in that decision's bounded detached abort-aware executor with at most four async CSPRNG attempts; transition/disconnect takes its exact cancellation/finalizer branch and late completion is discarded. Before D17 closes, allocation/transport is not activated. Missing/invalid/paused/saturated entropy, capacity failure, or clear failure omits metadata, releases only bounded state, and never retries or affects the prompt or workspace operation.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: No renderer `uiActionSeed` reaches the prompt wire before the server prompt log-removal fence and wire attachment ship atomically. Prompt-family server ingress and token-bearing renderer ingress call no console/debug/logger/redactor/formatter/stringifier or logging executor with raw, parsed, type, rejection, error, or seed material. After original handling, observability is only a module-private saturating counter selected from a closed compile-time type/outcome enum; it contains no values, has no callback, is fixed O(1), serializes/persists nothing, and cannot backpressure. Parse/route rejection increments only fixed counters. Static bidirectional inventory and zero-call sentinels fail on a new logger/serializer/error path or provenance wire field.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: After operational prompt validation starts the source command, the server treats `uiActionSeed` as untrusted and performs only the fixed-schema nonrecursive SPEC-34 extractor: maximum depth 4 from the seed, 207 charged own-data property reads including the message seed, array length, and 32 indexed element descriptors, 170 scalars, 32 subjects, an exactly enumerated 1,034-step ceiling, and 16,384 UTF-8 output bytes. Each private seed subject carries its required strictly increasing original operational attachment index. Target evidence is direct-read only at those positions from the already-required validated attachment vector and becomes at most 32 exact five-field null-prototype data copies with separate 129-property/160-scalar/exact 901-step/16,384-byte caps. Gaps are allowed; duplicates, reordering, holes, out-of-range/non-accepted entries, or type/path mismatch omit UI provenance. The indices/ordinals are stripped before canonical construction. No map/key scheme, scan, handle, attachment/vector entry, callback, capability, operation object, or graph reference enters the queue. Structural/budget/preflight/direct-read failure yields only fixed `ui_provenance_seed_unavailable`, submits no UI candidate, and leaves the prompt unchanged. The bounded seed/target copies enter D01 only with the bound context below; D01 accounts and releases all three on every terminal/cancellation/expiry/saturation/cleanup/shutdown branch.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Ledger storage should include validation status, edge/resource projections, and indexes for workspace, resource/path, event family/type, thread, turn, tool call, UI action, harness ID, harness run, harness event, automation run, audit query, correlation ID, causation ID, root/parent event ID, edge endpoints, and timestamp range. Trigger/script/scheduler/agent subtype indexes exist only if `AUT-D03` approves the corresponding fields and selectors. Provider-native IDs can be indexed inside provider-keyed `nativeRefs` or provider-specific payloads when a harness adapter needs replay or dedupe queries. Payload hashing and redaction rules are required before broad snapshot, diff, or tool-output persistence.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Open owner decision `LED-D01` blocks SPEC-35b/SPEC-40c payload hashing and historical ledger capabilities, not first-package resource/render work. It must approve deterministic payload serialization/canonicalization, byte encoding, algorithm/digest representation, hash policy/version storage, and migration/reverification semantics. It is distinct from ULV-D10 content/snapshot/diff/tool-output hashing.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Open owner decision `LED-D02` blocks SPEC-40b2e and every canonical `eventFamily: 'ledger'` producer. It must decide whether ledger-internal maintenance/repair/migration/audit events are needed and, if so, define exact event/phase/lifecycle branches, producer/domain identities, actor/provenance, private row-key boundary, accepted relationships, redaction/failure behavior, deterministic bounds, ordering/dedupe/replay/migration, and fail-open tests. Ordinary storage of other accepted event families remains independent.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Open owner decision `LED-D03` blocks every durable `caused_by` edge. It must define the exact event-type/pointer/domain matrix, which `provenance.confidence` values qualify, pointer/confidence consistency validation, correlated/inferred/unknown evidence handling, duplicate/conflicting causes, and deterministic rejection tests. Accepted refs or hashed historical capabilities prove endpoint identity only, not causal meaning. Indexes and approved non-causal edges may proceed.

vocabulary.text: Open owner decision `LED-D04` blocks production Slices 35b-35d. It must define exact natural/idempotency keys and unique constraints for every ledger table; event/child transaction boundaries; duplicate/conflict behavior; whether detached retry/defer exists and its queue/item/byte capacities, attempts, backoff, cancellation, shutdown/restart/replay semantics; permanently missing targets; database nonsettlement; terminal fixed diagnostics; and crash/concurrency/source-isolation tests. No inline retry or unbounded deferred work may be implemented. Slice 35a inventory remains independent.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Open owner decision `UEB-D01` blocks SPEC-40a/40b1a and the first Wiki/File packet. It must define exact admission/listener executor item and byte capacities, concurrency and producer/subscriber fairness, enqueue/eviction/drop behavior, cancellation finalizers, per-task event/context/ref retained-byte and lifetime caps, never-settling isolation, and listener saturation behavior. Byte accounting must define measured representation/encoding, object/container overhead, shared-event/context/ref apportionment, queued/active/cancelling ownership, charge/release transition points, cap precedence, and bounded cap-plus-one measurement. Every command has a bounded private owner cell whose atomic `open_empty|open_slot -> closed` transition makes completion/cancel/throw win safely over late installation; initialization failure disables only provenance. UI preflight owns no slot/link until all bounded data is ready; nullable slot failure installs/offers nothing, install after close terminalizes/releases the new slot, and the fixed offer receives a successfully installed slot synchronously while only its D01-created link enters task ownership. D01 must separately define global owner-cell/live-slot count/byte caps, per-slot/per-producer lease caps, repeated acquisition, slot/ref/lease lifetime, and the private nonserializable `AcceptedRefSlotTaskLink` representation/item/byte charge, atomic link-creation/admission-or-finalization transition, single-settlement rule, partial-state release, leaked-cell/link/lease expiry/forced cleanup, slot-registry shutdown, restart, and fixed value-free overload/leak diagnostics. Slot/lease exhaustion returns absent/null and releases bounded provenance state. Link creation/measurement/setup failure, rejection, or overflow invokes only the internal fixed link finalizer, settles an installed slot once, terminates only provenance work, independently skips saturated listener deliveries, and never backpressures or retries a source operation. No queued owner cell/slot handle, caller callback, runnable, finalizer, command-context handle, capacity, accounting, or default is permitted; the packet cannot be assembled, frozen, approved, or handed to an orchestrator until this decision closes and the affected documents are back-validated.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Open owner decision `RSC-D17` blocks SPEC-32b0 token allocation/transport activation and the first Wiki/File packet. It must define exact global/per-connection token-metadata executor queue item/byte caps, concurrency/fairness, enqueue/eviction/drop behavior, cancellation/finalizer deadlines including abort-ignoring providers, per-job retained context/provider byte and lifetime caps, live-token binding count/byte caps and cleanup, shutdown/restart, and fixed value-free saturation diagnostics. Byte accounting must define measured job/binding representation/encoding, object/provider-wrapper overhead, shared-ref apportionment, queued/active/cancelling/live ownership, charge/release points, cap precedence, and bounded cap-plus-one measurement. Capacity failure only omits token metadata and releases bounded state; it never retries or affects init, transitions, panels, prompts, connection lifecycle, or source operations. No capacity/accounting/default is permitted.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Open owner decision `CHAT-D01` blocks SPEC-40b2a canonical chat registration and migration, not first-package resource/render work. It must define exact canonical event types and phase/lifecycle status/presence matrix; IDs, chat payload fields, mirrors, current-record identities, and accepted-only relationships; optional UI cause/result pointer bindings and non-wait behavior; redaction policy ID/version plus sensitive prompt/content/attachment/native-ref handling; failed-redaction safe-core versus no-event behavior; deterministic text/attachment/tool-summary/native-ref/array/serialized-byte bounds and truncation/omission/overflow forms; ordering, dedupe, replay, and idempotence; legacy coexistence/removal/backfill; finding 4's `chatResources` relationship to normalized `resources[]`; finding 8's derivation-versus-redaction-survival rule for `chat.hasToolCalls`; and fail-open tests. Until closure, current `chat:*` facts remain noncanonical, receive no canonical admission marker or `uiActionId`, and are not mutated or backfilled.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Open owner decision `AUT-D02` blocks a file-trigger automation fact from storing `automation.matchedEventId`, upstream resource root/parent/causation IDs, or a direct `triggered` edge. Because the operational watcher filter executes independently of canonical resource admission, D02 must define the private observation/run capability handoff, non-wait ordering, lifetime, exact pointer/selector, multiple-match and rename behavior, dedupe, late/missing/rejected/cancel/restart semantics, and exactly-once tests. Operational triggers continue unconditionally; only after AUT-D03 approves a base canonical automation fact may that fact proceed while omitting D02-blocked resource relationships.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Open owner decision `AUT-D03` blocks base canonical automation run/match registration, emission, accepted references, persistence, and any new production run-ID generator/ABI. The settled requirement is that eventual canonical automation facts contain durable `automation.runId` and `automation.kind`; D03 cannot remove those fields. It must define exact per-kind generation owner/timing/format and operational handoff; event/phase/lifecycle presence; subtype ID ownership/equality/presence; actor/source/origin/observer/context; sensitive trigger/schedule/condition/path fields and redaction policy/failure branch; deterministic bounds/overflow; ordering, dedupe, replay, restart, and cancellation; and fail-open tests. Slices 37a-37b may only audit existing IDs and prepare inert decision tables/ABI fixtures/tests; they cannot add/replace a production generator, expose a new ID ABI, or create canonical identity. AUT-D01 and AUT-D02 remain separate result and matched-resource gates.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Open owner decision `TOOL-D01` blocks SPEC-40b2b `chat.tool.args|result` registration and corresponding persistence, not first-package resource/render work, SPEC-36a evidence gathering, or preparatory harness identity/native-ref work. Jointly with `AUT-D01` and finding 3, it must select the unified captured-output extension contract—including whether it is one shared block—then define exact tool mapping; args/result/outcome domains; normalization/encoding; redaction policy IDs/versions, detection, shapes, omissions, failure-safe/no-event behavior, and safe resource extraction; hash/byte/truncation semantics; exit/signal/provider-error normalization into outcome/lifecycle fields; complete phase/outcome presence; external-artifact qualification without row-ID leakage; bounds and unavailable/partial/stream/error/cancel/timeout branches; and fail-open tests. Finding 4 separately blocks `toolResources` until its relationship to normalized `resources[]` is approved.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Open owner decision `TOOL-D02` blocks canonical harness identity and `chat.tool.started` registration, accepted refs, activation, and persistence. It must define exact event/phase/lifecycle presence; current-record harness/tool ID ownership/equality; actor/source/origin/observer; provider/native-ref allowlist and redaction policy/failure branch; deterministic bounds/overflow; ordering, sequence, dedupe, replay, reconnect, cancel; accepted-only chat/upstream relationships; and fail-open tests. Slices 36a-36c remain inert evidence/helpers.

vocabulary.text: Open owner decision `AUD-D01` blocks SPEC-40b2f audit-domain registration and SPEC-38b-38f, not first-package resource/render work or SPEC-38a evidence gathering. It must define exact versioned query/review/recommendation/ticket schemas and domain ownership; event/phase/lifecycle branches; typed/redacted filters; confidence and completed/failed/incomplete/unavailable/cancel semantics; accepted evidence/result presence; redaction policy/failure-safe behavior; deterministic hard filter/evidence/result/summary/recommendation/ticket/traversal/serialized-byte bounds, overflow diagnostics and pagination; and fail-open tests.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Open owner decision `ULV-D04` blocks storm detection, batch persistence, and compaction. It covers exact window/group/quiet thresholds; global active-window/workspace/key/member/timer/diagnostic/reconciliation/in-memory capacities; hard capacities for every persisted storm array, summary, edge, batch row, diagnostic, and serialized byte budget; deterministic admission/coalescing/eviction/expiry/cleanup/selection/deduplication/truncation; first/last preservation; overflow counters/flags and follow-up discoverability; crash/restart semantics; byte measurement; cap precedence; and configuration ownership. Unique-key/sustained-load overflow cannot suppress or delay source facts, drop artifacts before accepted 35f, or create false attribution. No implementation may invent defaults or call either detector or summary bounded before approval.

vocabulary.text: `ULV-D03` and `ULV-D05` also block metadata/hash-only file-version rows, not only content artifacts or storms. D03 must decide eligibility for any row across file type/size/class and metadata-only exclusions; D05 must decide retention/deletion for metadata rows, edges, and indexes as well as snapshots/diffs/blobs. Non-batch metadata/hash-only registration/emission additionally requires `ULV-D10` and `ULV-D12`; content persistence has its further named blockers.

vocabulary.text: Renderer cache invalidation should use a transport-specific message such as `resource:invalidate`, not reuse canonical resource event identity for `resource:*` bus-topic or WebSocket/cache semantics.

vocabulary.text: Before canonical `workspace:switched` is enabled, SPEC-32b0 atomically moves the active operational transport to permanent private `workspace:operational_switched`, installs coordinator-authoritative workspace/root resolution plus cache-only session projection and synchronous baseline broadcaster recovery, removes workspace switching from the old ledger whitelist, and proves all other old-shape paths are moved or fenced. Healthy baseline renderer notification is exactly one; failure is at-most-once and converges through authoritative reconnect snapshot/recovery. This noncanonical, unpersisted transport is not awaiting a provenance retirement slice. Canonical lifecycle separately drives accepted-only facts and `resource:invalidate`. Neither bus shape may enter the other's broadcaster/subscribers, and canonical lifecycle persistence waits for SPEC-35.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Automation events use `automation.runId` and `automation.kind`; these two common-field requirements are settled, while AUT-D03 owns their exact generation ABI and all subtype ID ownership/equality/presence. Downstream resource events may reference the common identity through `provenance.cause.automationRunId` and, when approved for that event schema, compact `automationRef.automationRunId` / `automationRef.automationKind`, only from an accepted automation reference. Subsystem-specific IDs such as `triggerRunId`, `schedulerRunId`, `scriptRunId`, or `agentRunId` remain D03 candidates rather than settled secondary indexes.

vocabulary.text: Storm records should use the shared event envelope and preserve time range, affected paths, count, and representative safe metadata when available. Any embedded member cause/actor/resource ID requires an exact SPEC-39 target/source `acceptedPayloadPointer` builder binding against a live accepted ref or revalidated historical capability; whole-object copying is forbidden. Mixed-cause or mixed-actor storms omit a single top-level cause/specific actor and use separately proven summary entries. Representative hashes/snapshot/diff references require their later approved policies.

vocabulary.text: - Canonical publication accepts only a privately registered `PreparedCanonicalCandidate`. `prepareCanonicalCandidate` strips caller-supplied proof fields, consumes upstream refs, and privately proves each registered atomic accepted-only relationship group. A missing, copied, stale, forged, mismatched, wrong-workspace, or otherwise unbound proof omits the whole affected relationship group with fixed value-free diagnostic `accepted_relationship_unbound`; it does not suppress an otherwise valid relationship-free base fact or affect the source operation. Whole-candidate suppression is reserved for an invalid required fact core, an unsanitizable base after relationship removal, an unrelated final schema error, or UEB failure. Admission clones/freezes the safe event, binds its allowlisted identity to an opaque ref, and freezes one `{ acceptedRef }` context. Every D01-admitted listener task calls exact ABI `listener(frozenEvent, deliveryContext)` with the same event/context/ref; bare-ref argument two is invalid. UEB returns `{ published: true, acceptedRef }` before listener code. Identity-sensitive consumers require `assertAcceptedDelivery`. A false publication result exposes no event/ref/context and queues nothing. Legacy `emit()` is non-migrated only.

vocabulary.text: - Source commands never await admission or a ref. A private per-command slot exposes only leased non-blocking `peekAccepted()` to frozen-registry producers. vocabulary.text: `UEB-D01` is OWNER APPROVAL REQUIRED before SPEC-40a/40b1a or first-package assembly. It must define exact admission/listener executor item and byte capacities, concurrency/fairness, enqueue/eviction/drop behavior, cancellation finalizers, per-task event/context/ref retained-byte and lifetime caps, never-settling isolation, and listener saturation. Byte accounting defines measured representation/encoding, object/container overhead, shared-event/context/ref apportionment, queued/active/cancelling ownership, charge/release points, cap precedence, and bounded cap-plus-one measurement. Every command has a bounded private owner cell whose atomic `open_empty|open_slot -> closed` transition makes completion/cancel/throw win safely over late installation; owner-cell initialization failure disables only provenance. UI preflight allocates no slot/link until all bounded data is ready; nullable slot allocation failure installs/offers nothing; install after close terminalizes/releases the new slot; and only after successful install does the fixed module-private offer receive the branded slot synchronously. Only its D01-created link enters task ownership. D01 defines global owner-cell/live-slot count/byte caps, per-slot/per-producer lease caps, repeated acquisition, slot/ref/lease lifetime, and the private nonserializable `AcceptedRefSlotTaskLink` representation/item/byte charge, atomic link-creation/admission-or-finalization transition, single-settlement rule, partial-state release, leaked-cell/link/lease expiry/forced cleanup, slot-registry shutdown, restart, and fixed value-free overload/leak diagnostics. Slot/lease exhaustion returns absent/null and releases bounded provenance state. Link creation/measurement/setup failure, rejection, or overflow invokes the internal fixed link finalizer, settles an installed slot once, terminates only provenance work, independently skips saturated listener deliveries, and never backpressures or retries a source operation. No queued owner cell/slot handle, caller callback, runnable, finalizer, or command-context handle is permitted. No capacity/accounting/default may be inferred.

vocabulary.text: Canonical `workspace:switched` publication is gated on the SPEC-32b0 operational sequencer/topic fence. Generic EventBus listeners are unawaited, so every active switch/create/remove/ribbon ingress synchronously enqueues one intent before lookup or active-state reads. A single workspace coordinator resolves intents FIFO, captures `from` from the last commit, transactionally commits active registry/settings changes, updates memory only after commit, and sends the exact adjacent pair plus opaque ordered capability through a closed registry of audited bounded synchronous hooks that reject thenable returns. Synchronous I/O, unbounded CPU, user/plugin callbacks, and reentrant mutations are prohibited because an in-process function that never returns cannot be recovered. Controller/ribbon code cannot write active state or emit switches directly. The coordinator owns authoritative workspace/root resolution; per-session cache failure forces recomputation/snapshot rather than leaving A authoritative. The baseline broadcaster has no async enrichment/serialized queue and is at-most-once: healthy delivery sends exactly one `type: 'workspace:switched'`, while failure records a diagnostic and relies on reconnect authoritative snapshot plus `lifecycle:refresh_required` without retrying the pair. The watcher hook invalidates/installs synchronously and supervises detached close/ready/reconciliation without holding the FIFO. Hook throws, returned thenables, and detached background failure/nonsettlement cannot roll back the committed workspace, invoke provenance, or block the next intent. This workspace-owned transport remains noncanonical and unpersisted after 40b1b. The old ledger whitelist stops recording workspace switches, and legacy persistence pauses until SPEC-35. After accepted 32b/32c/40b1b, canonical `workspace.switched` independently carries the registered envelope to accepted-only subscribers and the separate `resource:invalidate` freshness path; only its durable row remains gated on SPEC-35. Concurrent-request/failure tests prove one total order, adjacent pairs, database/memory/coordinator-resolver/watcher-generation consistency, healthy exactly-one notification, recovery after failure, and no canonical lifecycle row before SPEC-35.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: Workspace watcher and TRIGGERS.md filter lifecycle is a synchronous hook of the permanent private `workspace:operational_switched` coordinator dispatcher, not canonical lifecycle admission or generic EventBus ordering. Slice 32e is blocked until owner decision `RSC-D16` approves the exact close-diagnostic/readiness/reconciliation watchdog values and semantics. The hook verifies the next ordered capability/pair, invalidates the prior generation, installs B/null bindings/listeners, launches supervised close/ready/reconciliation plus watchdogs, and returns a non-Promise acknowledgment. Those tasks/timers check currency; throw or expiry cannot block the next workspace intent, current ready/reconciliation failure enters `degraded_recovery_pending` with exactly one freshness recovery, and close expiry only diagnoses cleanup. A later transition cancels/invalidates them. File-change trigger matching consumes only its single established workspace-watcher observation path; mutation handlers do not invoke a second matcher. It never awaits canonical resource admission. While `AUT-D02` is open, canonical file-trigger automation facts omit direct resource IDs/edges; after closure only its approved non-wait accepted-ref handoff may bind them. Provenance failure cannot suppress or duplicate operational trigger execution.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: The operational matcher accepts only this closed current watcher-condition vocabulary: `filePath`, `parentDir`, `type`, `ext`, `basename`, `delta`, `oldPath`, `newPath`, `parentStats.files|folders`, and `fileStats.lines|words|tokens|size`. The exhaustive lexer is owned by SPEC-32: 512 UTF-8 bytes overall; numeric keys use signed safe base-10 integers without plus/negative-zero/leading-zero/float/exponent; string keys use equality/inequality with a 256-byte quote-without-escapes value or `[A-Za-z0-9_./:@*-]+`; the three nullable keys also accept exact null. Operators parse longest-first and the full input is consumed. Watcher stats are operational trigger context, not canonical provenance enrichment. Slice 32e side-effect-free parses/classifies all blocks but validates/reloads only file-change blocks through atomic `replaceFilters`; cron and bus triggers retain one-time registration and cannot be duplicated/removed by workspace reload. Workspace parse failure installs no old-root filters; same-workspace fatal reload retains the last valid set. Invalid file syntax never defaults true. Post-execution provenance may use valid metadata only for correlation.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

vocabulary.text: File-change blocks also use SPEC-32's closed schema. Slice 32d only preserves the single current matcher; Slice 32e exclusively introduces and owns lifecycle repoint/recompile. It loads immutable declarative/programmatic base descriptors once, then instantiates both base and trigger filters per controller-owned generation capability with an opaque bound workspace root and currency guard. At the synchronous transition linearization point, after authoritative workspace selection and before any await, B/null becomes current and A is permanently invalidated. Programmatic filters with workspace side effects are generation factories. Actions recheck currency after every await/callback boundary and immediately before irreversible effects; stale callbacks/timers and obsolete reconciliation are no-ops. B handlers attach before transition awaits, settlement requires A close/B ready/current-generation reconciliation, and reconciliation never synthesizes trigger execution. Atomic replacement preserves each base descriptor once without retaining startup-root closures, replaces workspace trigger filters, and never touches cron/bus registrations. Tests prove every B action targets B and paused A callbacks cannot affect A or B after transition.

No renderer/client/session/operation/raw correlation is copied as fallback. Raw event/causation IDs in mutable session/operation state never qualify. Unknown legacy renderer relationship-ID fields are discarded. After successful workspace binding, missing optional UI details may remain null/unknown without blocking the command. Missing/stale/forged/wrong-connection binding or root/target mismatch creates no canonical `ui.action`, ID, ref, mirror, or edge and reports only exact frozen `{ code: 'workspace_context_unbound' }` to the dedicated one-key, process-memory counter sink; no token, path, workspace, connection, transition, attachment, reason, or exception value is retained. vocabulary.text: The private token is exact `wctx_` plus 43 base64url characters generated from 32 CSPRNG bytes. Init/switch may carry an already-available top-level token but never calls or awaits entropy; otherwise detached asynchronous allocation later sends exact recipient-only `workspace:context_token` with workspace ID/root/token. Panel config only echoes an already-installed token and never replaces it. Absence is degraded metadata and never blocks workspace/panel handling. The renderer owns exactly one module-private memory-only slot keyed by the current WebSocket object, outside Zustand, workspace/panel/view caches, state pushes, local/session storage, IndexedDB, URL/history, Electron persistence, and serialized snapshots. Every init/switch clears before optional install; the metadata update installs only after exact current socket/workspace/root equality; close, explicit disconnect, replacement, and shutdown clear synchronously before another prompt read. A prompt reads only for the exact current OPEN socket, so a new connection starts null and stale workspace state cannot restore a token. The allocator checks all live tokens and makes at most four abort-aware async CSPRNG attempts; rejection/collision consumes one, context change aborts/discards late completion, and exhaustion sends nothing with fixed value-free diagnostic. Two connections never share a bound token, and shared broadcaster objects/buffers contain none. Prompt echo is accepted only at `uiActionSeed.workspaceCommandContextToken`; the UI envelope itself never contains it. Other, inherited, duplicate, malformed, array, or alternate nested locations are ignored by runtime binding. Token-bearing inbound messages have no payload/type logger path; only a fixed private counter increments after original handling.
vocabulary.disposition: reconcile current/target/proposal with topic authority; remove ephemeral dependency

Byte accounting defines measured job/binding representation/encoding, object/provider-wrapper overhead, shared-ref apportionment, queued/active/cancelling/live ownership, charge/release points, cap precedence, and bounded cap-plus-one measurement. Unadmitted, evicted, cancelled, expired, saturated, or otherwise failed work installs/sends nothing, releases only bounded state, and never retries or affects init, transitions, panels, prompts, connection lifecycle, or source operations. No capacity/accounting/default may be inferred.

vocabulary.text: The server independently treats the seed as untrusted. Each private subject carries its strictly increasing original operational attachment index. Target evidence is direct-read only at those positions from the already-required validated attachment vector and becomes at most 32 closed five-field null-prototype data copies under separate 129-property/160-scalar/exact 901-step/16,384-byte caps. Gaps are allowed; duplicate/reordered/out-of-range/hole/non-accepted/mismatched entries omit provenance, and indices/ordinals are stripped before canonical construction. There is no key/map scheme or scan, and no handle, attachment/vector entry, callback, capability, operation object, or graph reference enters the queue. Structural/budget/preflight/direct-read failure emits fixed `ui_provenance_seed_unavailable`, schedules no UI candidate, allocates no slot/link, and cannot affect prompt acceptance/response. Those bounded seed/target copies enter D01 only with the bound context below; all three data values are byte-charged and released whenever an offer is attempted.
